subject: [PATCH v1] memcg: fix cacheline contention between lruvec stat updates and LRU lists

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Shakeel Butt requested additional testing on a non-Intel machine and suggested applying a different patch on an Intel machine to verify if it resolves the issue.

Reviewer Shakeel Butt suggested rearranging the fields in `struct mem_cgroup_per_node` to reduce cacheline contention between lruvec stat updates and LRU lists, specifically by moving the `orig_objcg` and `objcg_list` fields to a separate cacheline group (`memcg_pn_cold`) that is only touched when the memcg is reparented or freed.

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This patch addresses cacheline contention between lruvec stat updates and LRU lists by modifying the update paths to avoid accessing struct mem_cgroup_per_node directly. Instead, it uses the memcg to access the per-cpu lruvec stats, reducing unnecessary cache line fetches and contention on the lru_lock critical section. The patch was motivated by analysis of perf c2c output showing high contention on the first 64 bytes of mem_cgroup_per_node, even though there were no writes to it. The fix is expected to improve performance in multi-threaded workloads with many threads faulting in pages in a single memcg.
